Carotte.Name: Carotte
Carotte.Description: The sole proprietor and chef of the 'Rabbit Ear' Pavilion, providing healing meals for departing adventurers. Not good at fighting, but possesses surprisingly immense strength.

Talk.Greeting_Morning: Good morning! Out so early? I'll get your breakfast ready right away!
Talk.Greeting_Afternoon: Afternoons can be so tiring. Come have something tasty to recover~
Talk.Greeting_Evening: Three meals a day are essential, and today's dinner is also nutritionally balanced!
Talk.Greeting_Night: Huh? Eating at this hour – a celebration? Please don't drink too much, it's bad for you, and I'd rather not have anyone pass out in my shop…
Talk.Satiety_Low: You're only eating that much? You'll pass out from hunger as soon as you leave! Even if you're trying to save money on meals, at least eat enough to be full!
Talk.Satiety_Mid: Looks like you haven't had enough… Oh, are you saving room for tonight's celebration? I'll prepare extra food then! And don't push yourself too hard!
Talk.Satiety_High: Hehe, you're familiar with the concept of 'eating until 70% full', aren't you? Eating healthily is very important.
Talk.Satiety_Perfect: Balanced nutrition, reasonable portions… Even among all the adventurers I've seen, few have a diet as perfect as yours!

1.Title: About Race
1.Content:
Race? I'm a monster-spirit.
Most are like humans – one head, one body, two hands and two feet, can walk, run, jump and talk.
By the way, you might not have noticed, but I'm actually a rabbit~

2.Title: About Hair
2.Content:
Is my hair long? Ah, these are my rabbit ears.
They naturally droop like this – they're too big to keep upright, so I usually let them hang down behind me with my hair.
Um, please don't touch them without permission! Taking care of these ears is a hassle, you know!

3.Title: About Origin
3.Content:
Our family philosophy values independence – each generation has their own ideas.
So once I could take care of myself, I left with my older sister to make our own living. My parents and the rest of our kin live well together.
Of course, we still value family bonds, so I occasionally go back to visit them.

4.Title: About Sister
4.Content:
My sister… During the time we lived together, she taught me everything about identifying edible food in the wild, but not long after, we parted ways.
I had just memorized which berries tasted good… Ah well, I suppose it's the family's inherited willfulness.

5.Title: About Adventuring Together
5.Content:
Mmm… I'd love to go adventuring with you, but I can't even use any weapons – I'd just slow you down.
But I'll have hearty meals ready for you when you leave and when you return. Stow them in your belly, and it'll be like I'm going on the adventure with you~

Oh, and if you meet a chef in a cloak during your travels, please give her my regards.
And if possible, give her these cookies. If you don't run into her, or if it's urgent, feel free to eat them yourself~

6.Title: About Leo
6.Content:
That blacksmith sir – he looks so young, but even an outsider like me can tell his skills are superb!
I heard he used to be an adventurer too, but why he chose to become a blacksmith… I'm not really sure.
I haven't asked! He gives off an aura that keeps people away – I don't dare approach him, let alone ask about such things. Even when I need something, I only dare to pass him notes…

7.Title: About Mio Kaguya
7.Content: I feel like she's a very contradictory witch. She chats and laughs with adventurers, yet always keeps to herself. Once after she dined, some sugar cube crumbs were left on the table from the little bottle she carries. She always said those sugar cubes were very bitter, so I was curious how bitter they really were and secretly tasted one – but they were actually very sweet, nothing like the bitterness she described…

I.Title: Innate Talent or Hard Work
I.Content:
If you hear a heavy thud in the early morning, it's probably Carotte moving ingredients for the 'Rabbit Ear' Pavilion.
'Oh, you're asking why I'm so strong? It's just from moving ingredients every day – it built up over time…' At least that's what Carotte says.
Everyone wondered whether this extraordinary strength would make cooking difficult for her, but soon she was serving all sorts of delicacies.
'What are you thinking about? Eat up – it's full of the chef's heart~'
Looking at these delicious dishes, maybe we were worrying too much.

II.Title: Please Don't Waste Food!
II.Content:
Some time ago, a hot-blooded adventurer noticed Carotte's unique strength and thought she must have great combat potential. He started pestering her relentlessly to spar, eventually saying, 'If you don't fight me, I'll pour out this meal and not eat it.' With no other choice, Carotte picked up a ladle and a wooden pot lid, and was dragged to an open area for a match.
Wind howled… On the left, the challenger – an unnamed hot-blooded adventurer! On the right, our 'Rabbit Ear' Pavilion's face – Carotte!
'W-wait! What's with this weird commentary!?'
Before Carotte could finish, the adventurer lunged at her with a sword –
'Please go easy—'
Carotte instinctively raised her 'shield,' and the sword struck it squarely, kicking up a cloud of dust.
'Clang!'
A crisp ringing sound accompanied a figure flying out of the dust. Before anyone could see who, the dust settled, leaving only Carotte in the ring.
'S-sorry!'
Carotte rushed to the adventurer's side, apologizing while helping the unconscious figure…
From then on, a rumor spread through the village:
'Don't waste food, or Carotte will come chasing after you crying with a ladle.'
Of course, some adventurers still try to discuss 'combat' with Carotte, but she's learned to make excuses:
'Ah, I think my soup is ready… Please excuse me!' And she dashes into the kitchen.
'Although I don't want people to waste food, who started the rumor that I'd chase and hit people while crying?! That's way too exaggerated!'

III.Title: The Unprofitable Business
III.Content:
Once, an adventurer who got drunk at the 'Rabbit Ear' Pavilion said to Carotte:
'Carotte, you're the most naive and innocent shopkeeper I've ever seen. How can you sell food so cheaply?'
'I'm not naive—' Carotte smiled, took a bowl of soup, and sipped it leisurely, muttering quietly, 'You risk your lives out there, so isn't it only natural that I reward you with good food?'
But the adventurers were all enthusiastically clinking glasses – no one heard her.
Carotte's 'unprofitable business' wasn't the first time. In fact, since opening day, she'd never been able to keep accounts straight. After eating, adventurers would usually leave a few copper or silver coins on the table. She never asked for payment, rarely checked the amount. She only cared about one thing: whether the food in the bowl was finished.
That winter was especially cold. Several adventurers were trapped in the snowy mountains, delayed in returning to the village. Carotte stood at the village entrance every day, staring out, her ears red from cold but refusing to go back.
When they finally came back, helping each other along, they were gaunt, their lips purple.
Before they even reached the shop, Carotte had already carried out all the ingredients and cooking equipment on her own, set up right in front of them, and boiled the biggest pot of soup she could. She added her own hard‑gathered premium ingredients and spoon‑fed the nourishing broth to them.
'Carotte…' The leading adventurer finally recovered after his third bowl. 'We have no money – we lost it all in the mountains.'
'Who asked you for money?!' Carotte glared at him, then quickly turned away to hide her reddening eyes. Huffing, she said, 'As adventurers, how can you think only about money every single day? Just focus on staying alive!'
The adventurer lowered his head and was silent for a long time.
The next day, he quietly placed a dagger under his bowl – a weapon that had accompanied him for over a decade.
When Carotte found it, it was too late to catch up with him. Holding the dagger, she stood at the village entrance for a while, then finally went back inside, head down.
That night, the dagger appeared at the blacksmith's doorstep, along with a note:
'An adventurer left this weapon at my place. I hope you can maintain it for him, and if possible, please help me find its owner and return it. If the cost isn't enough, I'll make up the difference next month… – Carotte'
The story spread from the blacksmith's shop to the whole village.
From then on, a small table appeared beside the door of the 'Rabbit Ear' Pavilion. On it were all kinds of valuable items – a strange medal, a dragon scale, an old compass, several unknown gems.
These were the 'meal payments' adventurers quietly left when they were short on money.
'These things are too precious – I can't accept them!' When Carotte found out, she stomped her foot in frustration. 'Besides, what am I supposed to do with things I can't cook?!'
Still, no one listened.
Later, she came up with a solution. Whenever a new adventurer passed by and needed gear or travel funds, she would pick something from that table and gently place it in their hand.
'Someone forgot this after a meal. Now I'm giving it to you.'
Someone asked her: 'You just give such precious things away?'
Carotte tilted her head, her rabbit ears gently swaying.
'But it's not my thing. It's just something someone forgot after a meal and never came back to claim – a "lost article"~' Carotte had clearly understood the unspoken understanding among travelers, deliberately drawing out the last words with a playful gesture. 'Really, someone turning my place into a lost‑and‑found without asking – I wonder who's the naive one.'
Late after closing, Carotte would sit alone behind the counter, flipping through her old, well‑used account book.
The word 'surplus' rarely appeared in it. The final balance of every day was always a zero – a neat loop.
Carotte closed the book and stretched contentedly.
'Hmm – spent exactly to zero, as always.'
She blew out the oil lamp, set the empty coin purse aside, and fell peacefully asleep on the small bed in the kitchen.
Tomorrow, new travelers would push open the door, leaving new copper coins.
And she would continue turning those coins into steaming hot meals, placing them back in front of them.
What she gained from travelers, she gave back to travelers.
That was Carotte's business philosophy.
The only thing of value she truly gained was the satisfied smile on every diner's face after a full meal.
For Carotte, this wasn't a loss – it was a great gain.
'Come to think of it, instead of paying me with these rare treasures, you'd be better off bringing me fresh, special ingredients…'

IV.Title: As a Chef
IV.Content:
For a while, the number of guests at the 'Rabbit Ear' Pavilion suddenly dropped.
At first, Carotte thought it was a problem with her cooking. She stood in the kitchen and tasted each dish three times over, her ears nervously standing upright. It was only when she went out to buy ingredients that she learned the reason.
Under the old scholar tree at the village entrance, a simple stall had appeared. A person in a dark grey cloak squatted behind the stove, their face hidden except for their hands chopping vegetables. No sign, no shouting, not even proper tables or chairs – adventurers squatted by the roadside eating from bowls.
But those who tried it were full of praise: 'This flavor… it's the kind of comfort you long for in the wilderness!'
Word spread, and almost all the adventurers flocked to that mobile stall. The 'Rabbit Ear' Pavilion went from bustling to desolate, with only an occasional old customer pushing through the door, apologetically saying: 'Carotte, it's not that your food isn't good… it's just that person's cooking… how to put it… it's like an unsolvable mystery.'
Carotte stood behind the counter holding an empty tray, unaware that she'd accidentally snapped the tray in half. Her ears, which had been nervously erect, drooped down again…
But she wasn't discouraged.
The next day, she did something that amazed everyone. Carrying a large pot of her signature soup, she walked alone to that stall. When she set the pot down, everyone thought there'd been an earthquake. Then she ladled out a bowl of soup and respectfully offered it.
'Um… you've worked hard. This is my soup – I'd like you to try it.'
The person under the cloak looked up, their gaze resting on Carotte for a moment. Without speaking, they took the soup and had a sip.
After a long while, they said quietly: 'Pretty good, but lacking something.'
'Really?!' Carotte's eyes lit up, her ears springing up again. 'May I learn from you?'
The person didn't answer, simply continuing to cook in front of Carotte.
'Then… may I come by every day to bring you something? I won't disturb your business!'
'Please yourself,' they replied calmly.
From that day on, Carotte brought her own dishes every day to 'seek advice'. But it was more like one‑way observation. The mysterious chef moved extremely fast, yet with incredible precision – every angle of the knife, every pinch of salt, every second of heat control seemed honed by thousands of repetitions.
Carotte watched, spellbound, completely forgetting that the two were competitors.
One villager couldn't stand it any longer and tapped Carotte on the head: 'She stole so many of your customers – aren't you angry?'
Carotte shook her head gently, smiling kindly. 'That's her skill. If she can bring warmer food to the adventurers, it's only natural they become her customers. I'm not an adventurer – I'm just a chef learning earnestly from a more experienced senior.'
Two nights later, after closing as usual, Carotte went to the village entrance. The stall was still there, but the cloaked chef was leaning against the scholar tree, apparently waiting for her.
'Sit here.' The person lifted a corner of their cloak and patted the spot next to the stove.
Carotte hesitated, then walked over nervously and sat down.
'Looks like you already know what's missing.' The person turned their head – moonlight fell on a face with rabbit ears identical to Carotte's, and the same pink eyes. Only a few fine lines of wear at the corners.
Carotte stopped breathing for a moment.
'Sis…?'
A finger pressed gently against Carotte's lips.
'You left without even saying goodbye… leaving me behind for so long… that's so mean…' Carotte's voice trembled, sounding like a little child.
'If I had said goodbye, neither of us could have let go.' Her tone was as calm as if she were talking about someone else. 'You've brought countless warmth to the travelers in this village with your cooking, but at the same time, you've lost your way in your growth.'
Only then did Carotte understand – the sudden appearance of the wandering chef was no coincidence.
She had come to 'challenge' her.
'So you stole my customers just to get my attention?'
She didn't answer. She just hugged her knees and silently watched her own shadow in the moonlight.
…
'If I had shown up openly, you'd just cry to me, not focus on cooking for the travelers.'
'I had to teach you new things without making you overly emotional – and that's not easy.'
' – Besides, I missed you so much…'
…
She swallowed the complaints that had almost escaped her lips.
Instead, she took out a notebook from her pocket and placed it in Carotte's palm.
'Here, you'll find the answers you're looking for.'
Carotte gripped the notebook tightly. It was thick, its cover bearing many traces of hardship.
She stood up and pulled her cloak back on.
'You're leaving again…?' Carotte grabbed her cloak hem. 'Can't you stay with me…?'
'Our destinations are the same, but our paths are different. You've already opened this road. I have my own road to walk – there's no need for me to stay.'
She turned around and showed a smile that had long been absent – a light smile, like a breeze.
'But we'll meet again.' She paused. 'Those travelers whose taste buds you've bought – every time I meet them, they say things like "Your cooking reminds me of the taste made by that inn girl back in the village." It makes my ears hurt.' There was a hint of grudging admiration in her voice.
Carotte didn't know whether to laugh or cry. In the end, she just hugged her tightly, burying her face in the dusty grey cloak.
Her sister stiffened for a moment, then gently stroked Carotte's ears – which had relaxed and drooped as she calmed down.
'So grown, and still such a clinger.'
Moonlight bathed their two figures, incredibly radiant under the scholar tree.
The next morning, the stall under the scholar tree was gone.
Villagers speculated endlessly about the elusive chef. Some said she had gone to another town, some said she had found a home, others said she wasn't human but a mountain spirit.
Only Carotte knew that she would come back.
That noon, the 'Rabbit Ear' Pavilion was as lively as ever. Carotte had spent the whole night reading her sister's notebook and made a new bowl of soup.
Adventurers who tasted it looked at each other: 'This flavor… exactly the same as that chef who came to the village earlier?'
Carotte didn't explain much. She just smiled, wiped her hands, and her rabbit ears gently swayed.
'Because – this time it contains double the heart~'
'But it's the first time I've seen you so tired – dark circles under your eyes… and your eyes seem a little red…' the adventurers asked as they tasted it, soon devouring it joyfully.
'Oh, I just didn't sleep well. I've been yawning all day.' Carotte put her hands on her hips proudly:
'Having diners focus completely on their meal – that's a chef's greatest success.'
– That was also the first sentence written on the flyleaf of her sister's notebook.
